ObjectName.value: A general map of Turky in Europe, Hungary &c. By H. Moll Geographer. (with views:) Belgrade (and) Temeswar. (Printed and sold by T. Bowles next ye Chapter House in St. Pauls Church yard, & I. Bowles at ye Black Horse in Cornhill, 1736?)

Categories.value: David Rumsey Historical Map Collection|PD-old-100-expired|Scans from the Internet Archive/unverified|CC-PD-Mark|Scans from the Internet Archive|Books uploaded by Fæ|PD-old missing SDC copyright status|Images dezoomed by Fæ

ImageDescription.value:
Zoomable full resolution image available at davidrumsey.com.

This image 5580.027 is a part of image group 5580.000.

Hand col. engraved map with 2 inset views. Relief shown pictorially. Includes geographic notes.

Contains 62 hand col. double-page engraved maps (10 folding). Contemporary ink inscription on front blank endpaper. Newer full polished calf with original gilt-lettered red leather label. A few minor repairs. The Atlas Minor was first published in 1729 and reprinted in 1732. This ed. has new engraved title-page with contents and revised maps. The maps in the third ed. are similar to those of the 2nd, except that a number of the American maps contain added place names. Like most of Moll's works, the majority of the maps are undated, although the maps of Great Tartary (no. 32) and "The West Part of Barbary" (no. 41) are dated 1732. The deciding factor which makes this copy the 3rd. ed. is map no. 13 (Germany) which carries the added legend, "Lorrain was ceded to France A.D. 1736 ..." Includes 29 maps of Europe, 10 of Asia, 5 of Africa and 18 of the Americas, including the double-hemisphere world map (no. 1) and the map of America (no. 45) that show California as an island. The Rumsey Collection copy includes 17 extra inserted, uncolored, undated maps (13 folding, 2 manuscript), 7 of which deal with the West Coast of Africa, and 2 of which are manuscript maps of the harbors at Bahia, Rio de Janeiro, the mouth of the Amazon River and Straits of Magellan, all with captions and place names in French; 3 others are of Upper and Lower Canada. The 17 maps appear to have been taken from several later 18th century sources, and were probably extracted from Kitchen's Pocket Atlas, Child's Universal Traveller, the English ed. of Du Halde's Description of China, and other works. A folded world map shows George Anson's track on his voyage of circumnavigation in 1740-1744, and is probably from one of the numerous eds. of his Voyage. Includes folded descriptions from John Howell Books and the Argonaut Book Shop.

Phillips, 585; Tooley. Dictionary of mapmakers, p. 444; Tooley. Maps and map-makers, p. 55; Tyacke. London map-sellers, 1600-1720, pp. 122-123.

ImageDescription.value: Former Wagner house, former Zseravitz house. Listed, two two-storey merchant-burgher's houses, early classicist, built around 1820. The façade on the left has five axes, the façade of the right part of the house has seven axes with a gate on the ground floor. In its U-shaped courtyard, the fourth wing is newer. On its façade there is an inscription: 'Monumental / characteristic "Wagner House" rebuilt in neoclassical style at the beginning of the XIX century' - History: From 1840 János Ivánkovits had a glass shop here. In 1843 János Zseravitz owned wine, timber merchant and industrialist. Among tenants are military officers' apartments. In the 1860s, Antal Felmayer's spice shop To the Black Dog, on the left Groszmann and Guttmann linen and lingerie, next to it was the bag and tarpaulin shop of Ignác Joszefert and his partner, next to which first Rudolf Stampa, then Allemann and his partner's confectionery, Emil Glück's dance school. In 1865 it was still called Zseravitz House. In 1867 it was owned by Antal Felmayer Jr. The tenants of the 1870s were Felmayer, Groszmann Guttmann, Joszefert Ign and Allemann, Lipót Lőwinger's open silk and fashion shop, Károly David's Norinberg and haberdashery shop, Mór Hild's grocer, Károly Déry's law office, Sándor Politzer's jewelry shop. In December 1877 the building became the property of linen merchant Ferenc Antal Wagner. Tenants: József Neu, flour merchant and Emma Till, haberdasher. 1890s tenants Politzer and Till companies, Keglovich photographer's studio. In the early 1980s the house was renovated. In 1996 the shops were: the strudel shop Hatos strudel, Szeged Turist and the office of the National Philharmonic.
